column3: NASB renders “receive” as “accept” and “reasonings” as “opinions.”
NASB renders “believes” as “has faith” and adds “only.”
NASB follows the critical text; “despise” is rendered “regard with contempt,” and “received” is “accepted.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the Lord is able”); “will be upheld” is rendered “stand he will,” and “to uphold” is “to make him stand.”
NASB renders “judges” as “regards” and “fully assured” as “fully convinced.”
NASB follows the critical text without the Textus Receptus clause “he who does not regard the day, to the Lord he does not regard it”; it adds “does so.”

NASB follows the critical text (“died and lived again”) without “and rose”; “rule” is rendered “be Lord.”
NASB follows the critical text (“of God”); “despise” is rendered “regard … with contempt.”
The quotation is in capitals; “confess” is rendered “GIVE PRAISE.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “stumbling block or snare” as “an obstacle or a stumbling block” and adds “in a brother's way.”
NASB renders “persuaded” as “convinced” and “through itself” as “in itself.”
NASB follows the critical text (“For”); “is grieved” is rendered “is hurt.”
NASB renders “be denigrated” as “be spoken of as evil” and adds “what is for you.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text (“in this way”); “well-pleasing” is rendered “acceptable.”
NASB renders “edification” as “building up.”
NASB renders “destroy” as “tear down” and “eating through a stumbling block” as “who eats and gives offense.”
NASB follows the critical text without “or is offended or is weak”; it adds “to do.”
NASB follows the critical text (“The faith which”); it renders “keep to yourself” as “have as your own conviction,” “Blessed” as “Happy,” and “judging” as “condemn.”
NASB adds “his eating.”
